questions.q: Taking tax devolution and Finance Commission grants together as a share of the Centre's gross revenue receipts, which one of the following describes the pattern reported for recent awards?
o: A jump during the Fourteenth Commission's period, followed by a gradual decline through the first year of the Sixteenth
No change at all from the Eleventh Commission onwards
A steady rise in every award, peaking in the first year of the Sixteenth Commission
A fall during the Fourteenth Commission's period, followed by a jump under the Fifteenth
questions.e: Effective transfers rose from about 27-28 per cent under the 11th to 13th Commissions to 35.6 per cent under the 14th, then eased to 34.4 per cent and to 32.7 per cent in 2026-27 budget estimates. So a higher formal share need not mean higher actual transfers. The Centre also leaned on cesses and surcharges and trimmed its share in Centrally Sponsored Schemes, narrowing the States' effective gain.

questions.q:
With reference to consumer dispute redressal, as discussed in the Consumer Justice Report 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Disposal rates fell sharply below pre-pandemic levels.
2. As of 2025, nearly half of State Commissions lacked a sitting president.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is wrong: disposal improved after the pandemic, with 88.5 per cent reported, yet pendency still rose because of high inflows and vacancies. Statement 2 is correct and shows the gap between law and practice, since the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 contemplates disposal within three to five months. The Act provides a three-tier structure of District, State and National Commissions, and vacancies at the top directly affect benches.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 9-10; three-tier structure is static

questions.q: Which one of the following best states how conversion affects Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe status, as discussed around Chinthada Anand v. State of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Conversion ends both SC and ST status outright because both Presidential Orders carry the same religion bar
Conversion leaves SC status intact while a valid caste certificate is held, whereas ST status lapses automatically
Conversion ends SC status only when the person gives up the caste identity in writing, and has no effect on ST status at any time
Conversion to a faith other than Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism ends SC status outright, whereas ST status depends on whether tribal attributes and community recognition survive
questions.e: The SC Order carries a religion bar in paragraph 3, which the Court called absolute, and a caste certificate cannot override the fact of conversion. The ST Order, 1950 has no such bar, so the inquiry is fact-specific: customs, social organisation and acceptance by the community. A claim weakens if ties break, but it is not rejected automatically. This difference explains why Nagaland's Christian tribal communities remain Scheduled Tribes.

questions.q:
Challenges to anti-conversion laws usually rest on two lines of constitutional reasoning. Consider the following statements:
1. In Rev. Stainislaus (1977), the Supreme Court held that the right to propagate religion does not include a right to convert another person.
2. The privacy reasoning of Puttaswamy (2017) is invoked because a prior-notice rule exposes a personal choice of faith to the State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Stainislaus upheld early State laws, reading Article 25 as protecting the transmission of one's faith but not conversion by others, and public order was treated as a valid ground. Those challenging such Bills now rely on privacy and Article 21 liberty, arguing that a 60-day notice to the District Magistrate invites pressure and surveillance. The government's reply rests on reasonable restriction and public order.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 33-35; Stainislaus and Puttaswamy are static

questions.q: In the context of the Sixteenth Finance Commission, the term 'grand bargain' refers to a suggestion that
o: richer States fund poorer States directly in return for extra Lok Sabha seats
States give up GST compensation in return for permanent revenue-deficit grants
States accept a smaller share of a larger pool if the Centre folds much of its cesses and surcharges into regular taxes
the Centre takes over State debt in return for States adopting FRBM limits
questions.e: The idea addresses the Centre's growing reliance on non-shareable levies, which sit outside the divisible pool under Article 270 by design. Merging them into ordinary taxes would enlarge the pool, even if the share were lower. Critics say this dilutes the Commission's duty to fix the share objectively and that it did not criticise the surge in cesses. The other descriptions have no link with the Commission's proposal.

questions.q:
With respect to the privileges of Members of Parliament, consider the following statements:
1. A member may decline to give evidence in a court while the House is in session.
2. Freedom from arrest applies to civil cases during a session and for 40 days before and after it.
3. Freedom from arrest does not extend to criminal cases or preventive detention.
4. The press may publish truthful reports of a secret sitting of the House without prior permission.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 4 is wrong: the protection for truthful press reports does not cover secret sittings. Statements 2 and 3 are right, since the immunity exists so members can attend the House, and it is not a shield against criminal process or preventive detention. Statement 1 is right, tied to the priority of House business. Freedom from arrest and the right to decline evidence are individual privileges, while control over publication of proceedings belongs to the House collectively.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Setting up of the K. G. Balakrishnan Commission of Inquiry
2. Judgment in Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
3. Extension of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 to Buddhists
4. DoPT Office Memorandum on creamy-layer criteria
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Buddhist extension came in 1990, the Indra Sawhney judgment in 1992, the DoPT Memorandum in September 1993, and the Balakrishnan Commission in October 2022. Note the logical sequence between Indra Sawhney and the Memorandum, since the Court's creamy-layer direction led to the 1993 criteria. The sequence also shows how status and exclusion questions recur: first who is in the category, then who within it benefits.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Article : Subject
1. Article 122 : Validity of Parliament's proceedings not to be questioned for alleged procedural irregularity
2. Article 212 : Powers and privileges of State Legislatures and their members
3. Article 194 : Bar on courts inquiring into proceedings of a State Legislature
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 1 is right: Article 122 protects Parliament's internal procedure from judicial scrutiny for irregularity. Pairs 2 and 3 are reversed: Article 194 deals with privileges of State Legislatures and members, the counterpart of Article 105, whereas Article 212 is the State-level counterpart of Article 122. Learning them in two parallel sets, 105 with 194 and 122 with 212, avoids this common confusion.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Fifteenth Finance Commission set the States' share in the divisible pool at 41 per cent, a point below the Fourteenth Commission's figure.
Statement-II: Jammu and Kashmir had ceased to be a State following its reorganisation into Union Territories.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and linked. Fourteenth Commission's 42 per cent came down to 41 per cent mainly to reflect the fiscal needs of the new Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, which fell outside the States' pool. It was not a policy cut as such. The Fourteenth Commission's jump from 32 per cent had in turn offset the end of State Plan grants. The Sixteenth has retained 41 per cent as a semi-permanent norm.

questions.q:
After the Lok Sabha Speaker nominated its Committee of Privileges, the working of such committees came into focus. Consider the following statements:
1. When the Speaker refers a matter under Rule 227, the committee reports to the Speaker, who may pass final orders or have the report laid on the Table.
2. The Rajya Sabha's Committee of Privileges is headed by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha himself.
3. Where no time is fixed for the report, the committee must report within one month of the reference.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Rule 227 route ends with the Speaker, unlike a reference made by the House, which reports back to the House. Statement 2 is wrong, because the Rajya Sabha committee is headed by the Deputy Chairperson. Statement 3 is correct. The committee is semi-judicial, may summon persons and documents, and only recommends; the House can agree, disagree or modify the report.

questions.q:
The CAPF law of 2026 covers CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP and SSB. Consider the following pairs:
Force : Principal task
1. SSB : Guarding the India-Myanmar border
2. ITBP : Guarding the India-China border
3. BSF : Guarding the India-Pakistan and India-Bangladesh borders
4. CISF : Security of industrial undertakings and airports
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pair 1 is wrong: SSB guards the Nepal and Bhutan borders, while the Myanmar border lies with the Assam Rifles, which is not covered by the Bill. Pairs 2, 3 and 4 are correct. CRPF is the main internal-security force, and CISF works at public-sector units and airports. These are all under the Home Ministry, and the NSG, also excluded from the Schedule, has a specialised counter-terror role.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 9; force roles are static

questions.q:
Critics of State-level uniform civil codes raise federal and rights-based objections. In this context, consider the following statements:
1. Marriage, divorce, adoption and succession appear in the Concurrent List, so States are competent to legislate on them.
2. A State law repugnant to a Central law on a Concurrent subject can prevail in that State if it has received Presidential assent.
3. Articles 25 and 26 are the provisions usually invoked by those who see a code as a threat to religious autonomy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Entry 5 of the Concurrent List covers these personal-law subjects, which is the basis for Uttarakhand and Gujarat acting. Article 254(2) lets a repugnant State law prevail within that State once it receives Presidential assent, unless Parliament later overrides it. Articles 25 and 26 protect freedom of religion and denominational autonomy, and groups such as Naga communities cite them when voicing fears for their culture.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 6-7; Entry 5 List III and Article 254 are static

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India?
o: Licensing and registering food business operators
Prescribing labelling requirements for pre-packaged foods
Fixing the retail price of packaged food products
Setting science-based standards for additives and contaminants
questions.e: FSSAI regulates safety and information, and it does not control prices. Its functions include licensing and registration, standards for ingredients and contaminants, labelling such as the vegetarian mark and nutrition facts, inspections, and import control. It is also developing Front-of-Pack Labelling to curb ultra-processed food. Price controls lie elsewhere, for example under essential-commodity orders or legal metrology rules on declared prices.

questions.q:
With reference to the Sixteenth Finance Commission's approach to urban local bodies, consider the following statements:
1. It recommended that cess and surcharge collections be shared directly with cities.
2. A part of the funds is linked to conditions that include raising own-source revenue through property tax and user charges.
3. A one-time incentive is offered for merging peri-urban villages into urban areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is wrong: cesses are largely generated in cities but remain unshared and outside the divisible pool, a criticism made against the award. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. About 20 per cent of funds carries extra conditions, which hurts weaker cities. The Rs 10,000 crore merger incentive raises a federal concern since urban development is a State subject, particularly where rural local government is strong, as in Kerala.

questions.q: The Media Certification and Monitoring Committee (MCMC) was in the news in 2026 when political advertisements on electronic and social media were made subject to pre-certification. Which one of the following is correct about it?
o: It functions under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting and licenses television channels
It is an industry self-regulatory body formed by digital platforms under the IT Rules, 2021
It is a statutory body under the Press Council Act, 1978 that adjudicates complaints against newspapers
It is created by the Election Commission of India and also keeps watch on suspected paid news
questions.e: The MCMC is an Election Commission creation meant to enforce its guidelines during elections: it pre-certifies political advertisements and tracks paid news and misleading content. The Press Council deals with print-media ethics, the I&B Ministry grants broadcasting permissions, and platform self-regulation under the IT Rules is a separate mechanism. Candidates' spending on paid news also feeds into election expenditure scrutiny.

questions.q:
The 2026 notice against Speaker Om Birla followed rules that few motions have tested. With reference to a resolution for the removal of the Lok Sabha Speaker, consider the following statements:
1. Notice of the resolution is given in writing to the Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha.
2. The Speaker continues in office until the resolution is actually passed.
3. Earlier motions of this kind were moved against G. V. Mavalankar, Hukam Singh and Balram Jakhar, and none succeeded.
4. Notice of the resolution must be signed by the Leader of the Opposition.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Under Rules 200-203, notice goes to the Secretary-General, must state the charges clearly and needs the support of at least 50 members before discussion. The Speaker remains in office while the motion is pending. Only three earlier attempts were made, in 1954, 1966 and 1987, and all failed. Statement 4 is wrong: any member may give the written notice; the rules impose no requirement that the Leader of the Opposition sign it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A citizen cannot obtain a court order compelling the State to enact a uniform civil code under Article 44.
Statement-II: Directive Principles are declared fundamental in governance but are not enforceable by any court.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 44 lies in Part IV, and Article 37 says Part IV provisions cannot be enforced by any court, though the State must apply them in making laws. That is exactly why no writ can compel a uniform code, so the second statement explains the first. Courts have only urged Parliament, as in Shah Bano and Sarla Mudgal. Those remarks are exhortations and do not amount to binding directions to legislate.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 6-7; Article 37 is static

questions.q:
In the debate on sector-wise reform of personal law, consider the following statements:
1. Indonesia is cited as applying a single secular code to all citizens, Muslims included, in family matters.
2. The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 is a personal law available to Hindus alone for adoption.
3. The ICCPR is the 1979 convention on discrimination against women.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. Indonesia is cited as a harmonisation model, because it applies religious law to Muslims and a secular civil code to interfaith matters. The 2015 Act is a secular route open across religions, which is why it is suggested as the base for adoption reform. The ICCPR dates from 1966, and the 1979 convention is CEDAW. Both treaties are cited in arguments for gender equality in family law.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Case : Proposition associated with it in the UCC debate
1. Shah Bano Begum (1985) : Struck down instant triple talaq
2. Shayara Bano (2017) : Asked Parliament to frame a code while deciding a maintenance claim
3. John Vallamattom (2003) : A common code would aid national integration by removing ideological contradictions
4. Jose Paulo Coutinho (2019) : Treated Goa's civil code as a practical model
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are swapped traps. Shah Bano was the maintenance case in which the Court urged Parliament to legislate a uniform code, while Shayara Bano invalidated instant triple talaq. Pair 3 is correct: Vallamattom linked a common code with national integration. Pair 4 is correct: Coutinho held up Goa as a working model and said uniform law need not offend freedom of religion. Sarla Mudgal is another case often cited for gender equality.

questions.q:
The removal notice against Speaker Om Birla in 2026 revived interest in the office's history. Consider the following statements:
1. The titles Speaker and Deputy Speaker came with the Government of India Act, 1935.
2. The Government of India Act, 1919 led to the creation of such posts in 1921, then titled President and Deputy President.
3. The Speaker is chosen by a majority of the total membership of the Lok Sabha.
4. The date of the Speaker's election is fixed by the President.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statement 3 is wrong: election needs only a simple majority, which is a contrast with removal, which needs a majority of all then members. Statements 2 and 1 give the colonial lineage: President and Deputy President from 1921, with the 1935 Act changing the names. Statement 4 is right, and a pro-tem Speaker swears in members beforehand. Conventionally the candidate comes from the ruling party, though no special qualification is prescribed beyond membership.

questions.q:
In its March 2026 ruling, the Supreme Court also laid down tests for a person claiming SC status after reconversion. Consider the following statements:
1. Proof of original SC origin, of bona fide reconversion, or of acceptance by the caste community will suffice, any one being enough.
2. Once the claimant shows reconversion, the burden shifts to the State to disprove community acceptance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are wrong. The three conditions must be met cumulatively and conclusively, so any one alone is not enough. The burden of proof rests entirely on the claimant and does not shift to the State. Proof includes complete renunciation of the adopted faith and actual observance of the original caste's customs, rituals and obligations. The strict test guards against opportunistic claims to reservation or special-law protection.

questions.q:
Critics of the Sixteenth Finance Commission's horizontal formula raised several points. Consider the following statements:
1. The tax-effort criterion was dropped.
2. GSDP enters both through income distance and through the new contribution measure.
3. The contribution measure uses the square root of GSDP to temper it.
4. Sector-specific and State-specific grants were expanded to offset formula losses.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Dropping tax effort sits oddly with a stated focus on efficiency. GSDP works in opposite directions: lower per-capita GSDP raises a share through income distance, while higher GSDP raises it through contribution, and the square root is a judgement-based softener. Statement 4 is wrong: no State- or sector-specific grants were recommended, and critics say Article 275 grants could have equalised outcomes.

questions.q:
With reference to grants from the Union to States, consider the following statements:
1. Grants under Article 275 are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India for States in need of assistance.
2. Article 282 confines discretionary grants to cases recommended by the Finance Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 275 covers statutory grants-in-aid, charged on the Consolidated Fund and usually paid on Finance Commission advice. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 282 is the separate discretionary head under which the Union or a State may fund any public purpose, without a Commission recommendation. Critics of the 16th FC said normatively designed Article 275 grants could have equalised health and education standards and neutralised formula losses.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 45-47; Article 282 is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Speaker's salary and allowances do not have to be voted upon annually by the Lok Sabha.
Statement-II: Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, though it may be discussed.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Speaker's emoluments are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, and charged expenditure is non-votable under Article 113, although it can be discussed. That is exactly why no annual vote occurs, so the second statement explains the first. The design protects the office's independence from majority pressure. Similar charging applies to the President, judges of the Supreme Court and the Comptroller and Auditor General.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 14-17; Articles 112-113 are static

questions.q: Why did the Supreme Court, in its 2026 creamy-layer clarification, call the counting of parental salary for children of PSU and private employees 'hostile discrimination'?
o: Those children were judged on income while children of government employees were judged by post or rank, treating comparable candidates unequally under Article 14
The 1993 Memorandum had been issued without consulting the National Commission for Backward Classes as required by Article 338B
Salary income had been counted only for children of Group A officers, breaching the 50 per cent ceiling on reservation
Reservation was denied without a hearing, which violated the natural-justice protection in Article 311
questions.e: The vice was unequal yardsticks: government employees' children were assessed by status, others by salary, despite the 1993 scheme excluding salary. A clarificatory letter of 2004, which counted salary especially where PSU post equivalence had not been established, cannot add a substantive condition. The Court did not rest on the 50 per cent ceiling, Article 338B or Article 311. It ordered reassessment and supernumerary posts for affected civil-services candidates.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Women's share of Lok Sabha seats remains far below their share of the electorate even after the gender gap in turnout closed.
Statement-II: In recent general elections, women candidates have won at a lower rate than men candidates.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the peak share is about 14 per cent against roughly half the electorate. Statement-II is the trap: women's success rate has in fact been higher than men's, about 11 against 6 per cent in 2019 and 9 against 6 per cent in 2024. The problem therefore lies in access to party tickets, a nomination bottleneck, and is not one of electability. This is the central finding of the analysis.

questions.q: 'Sarnaism', mentioned in the debate over Scheduled Tribe status and conversion, is best described as
o: a reform movement within Christianity among the tribes of Nagaland
a customary land-tenure system of the central Indian tribes
a form of tribal self-government recognised under the Sixth Schedule
an indigenous tribal faith followed by Adivasi communities
questions.e: Sarnaism is an indigenous faith of Adivasi communities, centred on sacred groves, and it is seen mainly in the Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh region. It is relevant because STs may follow Christianity, Islam or indigenous religions without automatically losing status. Some Adivasi movements there want ST converts to non-indigenous faiths de-listed. It is not a Christian reform current, a land-tenure system or a Sixth Schedule governance form.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 31-33; sacred-grove link is static

questions.q:
With respect to the office of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution requires the Speaker to have served at least one earlier term as a member of the House.
2. A Speaker who is disqualified from membership of the Lok Sabha, for instance under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, vacates the office.
3. The Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha require the Speaker to belong to the ruling party.
4. The Speaker's powers flow from the text of the Constitution alone.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct: the first ground in Article 94 ends the office when the Speaker ceases to be a member, so disqualification under the 1951 Act has that effect. Statement 1 is wrong, since no qualification beyond membership is prescribed. Statement 3 is wrong: choosing the Speaker from the ruling party is only a convention. Statement 4 is wrong: powers also come from the Rules of Procedure and from unwritten parliamentary conventions, which supply residuary authority.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 14-17; Article 94 is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A person who has converted to Christianity cannot invoke the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 as a Scheduled Caste member, as held in March 2026.
Statement-II: The 1989 Act carries its own independent definition of Scheduled Castes, separate from the Constitution.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I follows from the ruling: conversion ends SC status, and so the Act's protection falls away along with reservation and other benefits. Statement-II is wrong, because the Act borrows the constitutional definitions and covers only those notified under Articles 341 and 342. It is this borrowing that makes the Presidential Order decisive, so the Act cannot be read more widely. The tension with continuing social discrimination against Dalit Christians remains for policy.

questions.q:
An analysis of six decades of election data was reported in March 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. In State Assembly elections, women's turnout overtook men's after 2011.
2. The largest number of women ever elected to the Lok Sabha came in the 2024 general election.
3. The number of women candidates fell between the 2019 and 2024 general elections.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is right: the gap in Assemblies turned positive for women after 2011. Statement 2 is wrong, because the peak was 78 women in 2019, with 74 in 2024. Statement 3 is wrong: women candidates rose, from 726 to 800. Together these show a rising supply of candidates alongside slightly fewer winners, an important pointer that parties and seats, not women's enthusiasm, are the bottleneck.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The privileges of Members of Parliament in India remain largely uncodified.
Statement-II: Article 105 exhaustively lists every privilege enjoyed by Parliament and its members.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: Parliament has never passed a codifying law, so privileges still rest substantially on British conventions and practice. Statement-II is wrong: Article 105 expressly names only freedom of speech and immunity for speech, votes and authorised publications, and it leaves other privileges to be defined by Parliament by law. Because the list is open-ended, critics argue for codification to protect free speech and press freedom.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 7-9; Article 105(3) is static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs relating to postal ballot categories:
Category : Example
1. Special voter : A State Governor
2. Absentee voter : An elector above 85 years of age
3. Service voter : A Union Cabinet Minister
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are right. Special voters are office-holders such as the President, Vice-President, Governors and Cabinet Ministers, along with spouses. Absentee voters include those above 85 and Persons with Disabilities. Pair 3 is wrong: service voters are armed forces and CAPF personnel and government servants posted abroad, while a Cabinet Minister is a special voter. The legal basis lies in the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961 and the RP Act, 1951.

questions.q: The Commission of Inquiry set up in October 2022 under former Chief Justice K. G. Balakrishnan was asked to examine
o: whether the creamy-layer principle should apply to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
whether Scheduled Castes should be sub-classified for reservation benefits
whether SC status can be given to persons converting to religions other than those allowed by the 1950 Order
whether reservation should be extended to minority educational institutions
questions.e: The Commission concerns converts to Islam and Christianity, a question also before the Supreme Court through a petition filed in 2004. The Centre opposes extension, relying on the 1950 Order and on the 'foreign origin' of those religions. Sub-classification and the creamy layer among SCs are separate issues dealt with in court rulings. Reservation in minority institutions is a different debate altogether and was not this Commission's reference.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Provision : Subject
1. Article 243I : State Finance Commission for Panchayats
2. Article 243Y : State Finance Commission for municipalities
3. Article 243W : Powers and functions of municipalities, linked with the Twelfth Schedule
4. Article 280(3)(c) : Finance Commission's duty on measures to augment a State's Consolidated Fund for its municipalities
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four are right. Articles 243I and 243Y are the twin State Finance Commission provisions from the 73rd and 74th Amendments. Article 243W empowers legislatures to devolve functions listed in the Twelfth Schedule. Article 280(3)(c) gives the Union Finance Commission the mandate behind ULB grants. The 16th FC's insistence on constituting SFCs and holding regular elections as a grant condition is grounded in these provisions.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 43-45; provisions are static

questions.q: 'Digressive proportionality', discussed as a way out of the North-South delimitation dispute, means that
o: larger States get more seats in total but fewer seats per person than smaller States
seats are allotted according to each State's share of Union tax revenue
seats are allotted strictly according to population at the latest Census
every State gets the same number of seats irrespective of population
questions.e: Digressive proportionality is a middle path. Representation still grows with population, but less than proportionately, so that small units get relatively more representation per head. Equal seats per State is the pure parity model used for the US Senate. Strict population allocation would reward higher-fertility States, which is the South's fear. A revenue-based allocation has no basis in constitutional design and would undercut one-person-one-vote.

questions.q:
With reference to Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992), consider the following statements:
1. It was decided by a Bench of five judges.
2. The Mandal Commission, whose report it examined, was set up under Article 340.
3. It upheld 27 per cent reservation for OBCs in Central government posts, subject to excluding the creamy layer.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is wrong: Indra Sawhney was decided by a nine-judge Bench, which is why its rulings still carry great weight. Statement 2 is right: Article 340 allows the President to appoint a commission on backward classes, and the Second Backward Classes Commission was headed by B. P. Mandal. Statement 3 is right, and the case also endorsed a general 50 per cent ceiling, save in extraordinary situations.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 41-43; Indra Sawhney details are static

questions.q:
In relation to breach of privilege in India, consider the following statements:
1. A newspaper editorial or a television interview by a non-member can amount to a breach.
2. A question of privilege can be raised only with the consent of the Presiding Officer.
3. For admissibility, the matter must be specific and of recent occurrence and need the intervention of the House.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three hold. Statement 1 is correct because breach includes acts casting reflections on members, the House or committees, whoever commits them; persons outside the House have been punished. Statements 2 and 3 describe the filter in the rules: the Presiding Officer's consent, and a specific and recent matter needing House intervention. Most notices are rejected, and penal action, from a warning to imprisonment, is rare.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Enactment) with List-II (Its reach):
List-I
A. Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937
B. Hindu Succession Act, 1956
C. Special Marriage Act, 1954
D. Divorce Act, 1869
List-II
1. Extends to Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs as well
2. Civil marriage for any citizen irrespective of religion
3. Marriage, divorce, inheritance and maintenance for one community
4. Dissolution of marriage among Christians
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The Shariat Application Act governs marriage, divorce, inheritance and maintenance among Muslims. Hindu codes such as the Succession Act also bind Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs, which is why 'Hindu' is a legal category wider than the faith. The Special Marriage Act is the secular route open to any citizen. The Divorce Act, 1869 applies to Christians, alongside the Christian Marriage Act, 1872. Together these show the plurality a uniform code would replace.

questions.q:
With reference to the Uniform Civil Code debate after Gujarat passed its Bill in March 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Gujarat is the second State after Uttarakhand to pass such a Bill.
2. The 21st Law Commission in 2018 recommended early enactment of a nationwide code.
3. The Special Marriage Act, 1954 already allows a civil marriage irrespective of the religion of the parties.
4. In Sarla Mudgal (1995), the Supreme Court stressed the need for a uniform code in the interest of gender equality across religions.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 2 is wrong: the 21st Law Commission said a uniform code was neither necessary nor desirable at that stage. Statement 1 is right, with Uttarakhand first. Statement 3 is right: the 1954 Act is the existing secular route open to any citizen, and reformers cite it to show that a common framework can sit beside personal laws. Statement 4 is right: Sarla Mudgal, a case of bigamy through conversion, stressed gender equality across religions.

questions.q: Findings on family permission, party ticket bias and voting autonomy among women, cited in the March 2026 debate on women's political participation, came from a 2019 survey on Women and Politics conducted by
o: National Council of Applied Economic Research
questions.e: The survey belongs to Lokniti, the research programme of the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies. It found that most women need family permission for political activity and that many perceive bias favouring those from political families. The Association for Democratic Reforms mainly analyses candidate affidavits, the NCAER is an economic research body, and the National Commission for Women is a statutory rights body and does not run this survey.

questions.q:
The press often uses 'no-confidence' for two different motions: the removal of the Speaker and the removal of the government. Consider the following statements:
1. Each requires the support of at least 50 members before it can be taken up.
2. A no-confidence motion against the government requires at least 14 days' written notice.
3. A no-confidence motion against the government rests on collective responsibility under Article 75(3).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: both need backing from 50 members under the Lok Sabha Rules. Statement 2 is wrong, because the 14-day notice is a constitutional condition only for removing the Speaker under Article 94(c). Statement 3 is correct: the government falls because the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the House. The two also differ on the required majority: effective majority for the Speaker, ordinary majority for the government.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 14-17; Article 75(3) and Rule 198 are static

questions.q:
The Supreme Court's 2026 clarification on creamy-layer exclusion drew on a long policy history. Consider the following statements:
1. Under the DoPT Office Memorandum of September 1993, salary income counted fully in the income and wealth test.
2. The concept of the creamy layer originated in Indra Sawhney v. Union of India.
3. The income ceiling, set at Rs 1 lakh in 1993, has stood at Rs 6 lakh a year since 2013.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 1993 Memorandum excluded salary and agricultural income, counting business, property and investment income; an October 2004 clarificatory letter introduced the confusion. Statement 3 is wrong: the ceiling, Rs 1 lakh in 1993, has been Rs 8 lakh a year since its 2017 revision. Post-based categories, such as Group A and B officers, decide most cases, and the income test works only as a residual mechanism.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Term : Description
1. Sujal Gaon ID : National digital architecture for the water sector
2. Sujalam Bharat : Unique ID given to each rural piped-water scheme
3. Har Ghar Jal : A scheme under the Swachh Bharat Mission for toilets
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: None is matched. The Sujal Gaon ID is the unique digital ID for source-to-tap mapping of rural schemes, and Sujalam Bharat is the national architecture it connects with, so pairs 1 and 2 are reversed. Pair 3 is wrong as Har Ghar Jal is the universal tap-water goal under the Jal Jeevan Mission, targeted for 2028. All three come under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

questions.q: The Supreme Court directed authorities to create 'supernumerary posts' for affected civil-services candidates in 2026. A supernumerary post is best understood as
o: a contractual post filled by lateral entry for a fixed tenure
an additional post over and above the sanctioned strength, created to accommodate a particular person or situation
a post that is reserved for officers on deputation from other services
a vacant post carried forward from an earlier recruitment year under the backlog rule
questions.e: Supernumerary posts sit outside the sanctioned cadre strength, so relief to wrongly excluded candidates does not displace those already appointed. That was the practical logic for about 100 candidates from CSE 2015 onwards. They are not backlog vacancies, which remain within sanctioned strength and carry forward. Nor are they deputation posts or lateral-entry contracts, which involve different recruitment and tenure arrangements altogether.

questions.q:
The Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Bill, 2026 deals with senior posts and the forces it covers. Consider the following statements:
1. All posts of Inspector General in the covered forces are to be filled by IPS deputation.
2. At least two-thirds of the posts of Additional Director General are to be filled by IPS deputation.
3. It responds to a 2025 Supreme Court direction to increase IPS deputation at the levels of DIG and IG.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct: at least 67 per cent of ADG posts, and all Special DG and DG posts, go to IPS deputation. Statement 1 is wrong: the share at Inspector General level is half. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2025 ruling had directed a progressive reduction of IPS deputation at DIG and IG levels within two years, which is why cadre officers see the Bill as running against that direction. It is an umbrella law on officers' service matters, earlier scattered across force-specific Acts.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Southern States fear that the next delimitation may reduce their relative weight in the Lok Sabha.
Statement-II: Under the Constitution as amended by the Eighty-fourth Amendment, the population for allotting Lok Sabha seats among States stays at the 1971 Census figure until the first Census after 2026 is published.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and linked. The 42nd Amendment froze inter-State allocation at the 1971 Census, and the 84th Amendment extended that until the first Census after 2026. Once the freeze lapses, seats would follow current population, favouring States with higher fertility and penalising those that controlled growth. So the end of the freeze is the very reason for the southern fear, along with the 'contributors versus beneficiaries' fiscal grievance.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 35-38; 42nd and 84th Amendments are static

questions.q:
In the context of food-safety regulation under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, consider the following statements:
1. Under the thresholds effective from 1 April 2026, a food business with an annual turnover of Rs 20 crore needs a State Licence.
2. Imported food gets customs clearance only if at least 60 per cent of its shelf life, or three months, whichever is less, remains.
3. The licensing changes of 2026 were made under regulations framed under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
4. The 2026 reforms are aligned with a NITI Aayog high-level committee on non-financial regulatory reforms.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 3 is wrong: the changes amend the 2011 Licensing and Registration Regulations made under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, not consumer law. Statement 1 is right: a State Licence covers turnover from Rs 1.5 crore to Rs 50 crore, with a Central Licence above that. Statement 2 is right, under the Import Regulations of 2017. Statement 4 is right. The aim is lower compliance cost for small businesses, though weak testing capacity, with only 266 laboratories, remains a concern.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Centre's actual transfers can fall as a share of its gross revenue even when the States' share in the divisible pool is unchanged.
Statement-II: Cesses and surcharges lie outside the divisible pool.
Statement-III: Revenue-deficit grants and State- or sector-specific grants, which also count as transfers, may shrink or end.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of Statement-II and Statement-III is correct and it explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Both explanations hold. A formal share of 41 per cent applies only to the shareable pool, so if more revenue is raised through cesses and surcharges, the States' share of total receipts falls. Grants are the other half of transfers, and the Sixteenth Commission discontinued revenue-deficit grants and gave no specific grants. This is why effective transfers can decline without any change in the headline figure.

questions.q:
The Supreme Court's March 2026 ruling on SC status and conversion turned on the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950. Consider the following statements:
1. The Order was issued by the President under Article 341.
2. Article 366(24) defines Scheduled Castes by reference to Article 341.
3. Once the first notification is issued, a caste can be added or removed only by a law of Parliament.
4. Buddhists were brought within the Order later than Sikhs.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. Article 341(1) lets the President notify castes State-wise or UT-wise, and Article 341(2) then reserves changes to Parliament. Article 366(24) makes SC identity a legal construct tied to that list, and this was central to the ruling. Paragraph 3 originally accommodated Hindus, with the Sikh extension in 1956 and the Buddhist extension in 1990, which is why the ruling treated conversion to other faiths as fatal.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 31-33; Article 341(2) is static

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
2. Fruit Products Order, 1955
3. Meat Food Products Order, 1973
4. Essential Commodities Act, 1955
Which of the above were consolidated into the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006?
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The 2006 Act consolidated eight earlier food laws and orders into one line of command, including items 1, 2 and 3. Item 4, the Essential Commodities Act, continues as a separate supply-management law; some food orders had been made under it, but the parent Act itself was not repealed and was invoked for LPG and gas in 2026. FSSAI, under the Health Ministry, now administers standards and licensing.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 7-9; ECA continuing is from Vision IAS pp. 35-36

questions.q:
Under the Maharashtra Freedom of Religion Bill, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. A court may declare a marriage solely for unlawful conversion null and void.
2. Children of such a marriage take the religion of the father.
3. Such children lose inheritance rights from one parent.
4. Offences under it are cognisable and non-bailable.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 and statement 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: children belong to the mother's original religion. Statement 3 is wrong: they keep inheritance rights from both parents, while the mother generally gets custody and maintenance is assured. Cognisable and non-bailable status gives police wide powers, which is why critics worry about the chilling effect on interfaith couples and consenting adults.

questions.q: The Sixteenth Finance Commission's proposed grant for urban local bodies for 2026-31 is well above the Fifteenth Commission's in rupees, yet commentators call it limited. Which one of the following best explains this?
o: The grant is paid only to municipal corporations of million-plus cities, leaving out smaller towns altogether
The grant replaces all spending by Central ministries on urban missions, so net transfers fall to nil
As a share of projected GDP the grant stays at roughly the earlier level, about 0.13 per cent, while urban needs and population grow
The entire amount is a loan to States repayable to the Centre within the award period
questions.e: The Rs 3.56 lakh crore looks large, but nominal GDP has grown too, so the ratio barely moves from about 0.12 to 0.13 per cent. Urban population is rising and cities generate about two-thirds of GDP. Grants are not restricted to million-plus cities, are not loans, and do not replace Central urban missions. Under-utilisation of earlier awards, from weak capacity and delayed State releases, adds to the problem.
questions.it: ULB grants as share of GDP
